findings.title: Redefining `self.downsize` overwrites the 5-argument version
findings.body: Ruby does not support method overloading by arity. Defining `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` on line 149 overwrites `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` defined on line 145. Any existing caller passing `(from, to, max_width, max_height)` (or 5 arguments with `opts`) will either pass `max_height` as `opts` (causing `TypeError: no implicit conversion of Symbol into Integer` when `opts[:allow_animation]` is accessed) or raise `ArgumentError: wrong number of arguments (5 for 3..4)`.

findings.title: Hardcoded 10MB client-side limit ignores `max_attachment_size_kb` and `max_image_size_kb` site settings
findings.body: Replacing `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` with a hardcoded `10 * 1024` (and similarly in `displayErrorForUpload` on line 246) bypasses configured site limits for non-image attachments (which are not downsized on the server) and blocks uploads larger than 10MB even when an administrator has configured `max_image_size_kb` or `max_attachment_size_kb` above 10MB.

findings.title: `gifsicle` does not support percentage geometry in `--resize-fit`
findings.body: `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails)` passes `"80%"` as `dimensions`. When `allow_animation` is enabled and the upload is a `.gif`, `OptimizedImage.optimize` invokes `gifsicle` with `--resize-fit 80%` (via `resize_instructions_animated`), which is invalid syntax for `gifsicle` (`--resize-fit` requires `WxH`, whereas percentages require `--scale`). `gifsicle` will exit with status 1 and the GIF will fail to downsize on every attempt.

findings.title: `tempfile.size` may return a stale cached value or fail to shrink for SVGs and failed conversions
findings.body: In the downsize loop, `OptimizedImage.downsize` neither checks the return value nor handles formats that `convert` cannot shrink (or SVGs/corrupted images where `convert` fails). When `OptimizedImage.downsize` returns `false`, the loop still runs all 5 attempts invoking `convert` repeatedly on the same file. Additionally, depending on the Ruby version/Tempfile implementation, `tempfile.size` queries the open file object whose state may not reflect external replacement by `ImageOptim`, so `File.size(tempfile.path)` should be used and the loop should break if `downsize` returns false or the file size stops decreasing.
